facts.statement: Neoaetosauroides was the first aetosaur discovered in the Los Colorados Formation, with remains found in the 1960s.
facts.quote: It was the first aetosaur known from the formation, with remains being discovered in the 1960s.

facts.statement: Fossils of Neoaetosauroides date to the Norian age of the Late Triassic and were found in the Los Colorados Formation in La Rioja, Argentina.
facts.quote: Fossils have been found in Los Colorados Formation outcropping along the Sierra Morada River in the Ischigualasto-Villa Unión Basin in La Rioja, Argentina, and date back to the Norian age of the Late Triassic.

facts.statement: Neoaetosauroides possessed two rows of dorsal osteoderms along its spine as well as ventral osteoderms.
facts.quote: Two rows of dorsal osteoderms run paramedially along either side of the spine. Ventral osteoderms were also present.

facts.statement: Unlike most other aetosaurs, the fourth finger of Neoaetosauroides was longer than the second and third fingers.
facts.quote: Unlike most other aetosaurs, the fourth finger was longer than the second and third.

facts.statement: The upper tooth row of Neoaetosauroides extended to the tip of its elongated snout, contradicting theories that other aetosaurs had keratinous beaks.
facts.quote: The upper tooth row of Neoaetosauroides runs anteriorly to the tip of the elongated snout, evidence that is incompatible with the theory of a keratinous beak proposed for other aetosaurs.

facts.statement: Biomechanical studies suggest Neoaetosauroides had a diet that diverged greatly from that of most other aetosaurs.
facts.quote: Biomechanical studies and muscle reconstructions of the skull of Neoaetosauroides have shown that it likely had a diet which diverged greatly from most other aetosaurs.

facts.statement: Neoaetosauroides possessed jaws that were somewhat weaker but faster than those of other aetosaurs.
facts.quote: Neoaetosauroides had somewhat weaker yet faster jaws.

facts.statement: Researchers proposed that Neoaetosauroides may have eaten a generalized diet of soft-bodied colonial insects and small vertebrates.
facts.quote: It was therefore proposed that Neoaetosauroides may have had a generalized diet of soft-bodied colonial insects, supplemented by small vertebrates.

facts.statement: Neoaetosauroides belongs to the subfamily Desmatosuchinae and the family Stagonolepididae.
Neoaetosauroides lived during the Norian stage, between 227.3 and 205.7 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Norian to Norian (227.3 to 205.7 million years ago)
